actor: Xet storage protocol engineer, Hugging Face Xet team
job: Building stall recovery inside the Xet transfer path itself — tighter stall detection, chunk-level resume and retry — rather than an exit to HTTP.
outcome: A stalled large-repository pull that resumes on the Xet path from its own partial chunks, with no cross-protocol handoff in the client default.
motivation: Xet is the product Hugging Face built to replace a plain file pull; a default bail-out would concede in shipped code that it fails.

task.who: Hugging Face Xet transfer protocol and client integration engineers
task.what: Ship chunk-level resume for interrupted Xet transfers
task.where: The hf_xet transfer client and its chunk cache
task.why: In-path resume removes the reason to leave Xet
task.how: Content-defined chunking with cached partial-chunk reuse

actor: Download path maintainer, huggingface_hub client library
job: Maintaining the download entry point that selects the Xet getter or the HTTP getter once, before any bytes move, and keeping that structure.
outcome: Released huggingface_hub versions where path selection stays a pre-transfer decision and no handler moves a live file between the two getters.
motivation: A mid-flight handoff discards partial state and restarts a terabyte-class file on the slower route, so it stays out of the default.

task.what: Keep getter selection a single pre-transfer decision
task.where: The hf_hub_download path and its Xet availability check
task.why: A mid-flight handoff would restart the whole file
task.how: Existing hf_xet-present branch plus the HF_HUB_DISABLE_XET switch

actor: Issue triage engineer, Hugging Face hub client and Xet support
job: Working the open stalled-transfer reports and routing each to a Xet-side fix or a retry gap, rather than to a cross-protocol feature request.
outcome: Closed stall reports whose fixes land inside Xet or in plain HTTP retry, leaving no shipped default that switches protocol mid-transfer.
motivation: The still-open report of a plain HTTP pull dying at 17.3 of 42.5 gigabytes shows the escape hatch is not more reliable.

task.who: Hugging Face hub client issue triage and support engineers
task.what: Resolve the open plain-HTTP no-retry download report
task.where: The huggingface_hub GitHub issue tracker and download tests
task.why: The escape route currently has no retry of its own
task.how: Reproduction on multi-gigabyte pulls with cache-state inspection

actor: Content delivery operations engineer, Hugging Face Xet delivery infrastructure
job: Raising throughput and cutting stall rate on the Xet delivery tier so long multi-shard pulls finish on the fast path they started on.
outcome: Measurably fewer stalled terabyte-class transfers, removing the operational pressure that would otherwise force a cross-protocol default into the client.
motivation: Faster infrastructure inside Xet is the fix the storage layer can ship without admitting the transport it built cannot carry its own artefacts.

task.who: Hugging Face Xet delivery and storage reliability operations staff
task.what: Cut stall rate on multi-shard weight transfers
task.where: Xet content-addressed storage and its edge delivery tier
task.why: Fewer stalls means no reason to ship an exit
task.how: Regional cache expansion with per-chunk transfer telemetry

actor: Release engineer, Unsloth model loading and transfer layer
job: Maintaining the automatic Xet-to-HTTP fallback shipped in 2026.8.2, keeping stall recovery in the project that receives the file.
outcome: A consuming library that recovers stalled pulls on its own, so the cross-protocol bail-out keeps living downstream of huggingface_hub.
motivation: A project built to fit training on smaller hardware spent a release making a download finish, because its users cannot wait for upstream.

task.who: Unsloth maintainers working the model loading and download layer
task.what: Harden the automatic Xet-to-HTTP fallback across weight pulls
task.where: Unsloth model loading code and its PyPI release train
task.why: Users need the pull to finish before upstream acts
task.how: Stall timeout detection wrapping the huggingface_hub download call

actor: Weight fetch maintainer, open-source inference serving runtime
job: Wrapping the hub download call with the runtime's own retry and protocol switch so a model server can start after a stalled pull.
outcome: Another shipped bail-out written by the receiver rather than the sender, which the prediction counts as confirmation rather than contradiction.
motivation: A serving runtime whose weight fetch hangs is a runtime that will not boot, and it cannot make that someone else's release schedule.

task.who: Model loading and weight fetch maintainers of the serving runtime
task.what: Add a caller-side retry and protocol switch
task.where: The runtime's model weight fetch and startup path
task.why: A hung fetch blocks the server from starting
task.how: Caller-side exception handling around the hub download entry point

actor: Model weight publishing lead, Alibaba Qwen release team
job: Opening the Qwen3.8-Max weights and the smaller 27B sibling into Xet-backed repositories, putting terabyte-class artefacts onto the fast transfer path.
outcome: Flagship-scale weights distributed through Xet, keeping the load that makes in-protocol recovery the fix Hugging Face invests in.
motivation: An open-weights launch is only a launch if the shards actually arrive, so the publisher wants the hub's own path to carry them.

task.who: Alibaba Qwen model release and distribution engineers
task.what: Publish the open Qwen3.8 weight shards to the hub
task.where: Hugging Face model repositories backed by Xet storage
task.why: Flagship weights only count once they download
task.how: Sharded safetensors uploads through the standard hub client

actor: Weight mirror operations engineer, regional model mirror service
job: Fetching reference weights once over the hub's path and republishing smaller derived artefacts, absorbing the stall risk on behalf of downstream users.
outcome: A mirror-side retry wrapper that finishes the fetch, adding one more receiver-written recovery instead of an upstream default.
motivation: The intermediaries who pull once and republish are the population that actually eats hours-long transfers, and they cannot wait on a client release.

task.who: Mirror ingestion and republication operations engineers
task.what: Wrap reference weight ingestion in a resumable job
task.where: The mirror's ingestion pipeline and object storage
task.why: Hours-long pulls drop and must restart cheaply
task.how: Scheduled ingestion jobs with per-shard checkpointing
